text:
elliot: quick heads-up — I found a deterministic KV-cache mismerge when async prefetch_kv + shard-merge happen in the int8-fused runtime on long contexts (~36k tokens). generates fine then at some point tokens repeat and later output drifts.
rana: repro please? is float16/FP32 affected?
elliot: float16/FP32 clean. repro attached below (small harness).

```
# minimal repro (local dev runtime)
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-int8-fused","input":"<long prompt ~36k tokens>", "prefetch_kv":true}' > out.json
jq .out[35940:35980] out.json
```

phil: logs? any warnings about memcopy/align or kv pointers?
elliot: log excerpt — shows a double-write to the same kv_ptr and then a short re-read that causes the decoder to consume an earlier token again.

```
[2026-01-07T18:09:21Z] INFO kv: write shard=3 kv_ptr=35956 seq=1478
[2026-01-07T18:09:21Z] INFO kv: write shard=3 kv_ptr=35957 seq=1479
[2026-01-07T18:09:22Z] INFO kv: write shard=3 kv_ptr=35957 seq=1480  # unexpected duplicate ptr
[2026-01-07T18:09:22Z] WARN kv: merge: shard3 seq_gap=1
[2026-01-07T18:09:22Z] INFO decode token=35958 kv_ptr=35957  # decoder reuses stale entry
```
rana: interesting. double write at same ptr suggests a race between the prefetch thread and the main writer or a missing atomic increment on the shard pointer. is this only when prefetch_kv=true?
elliot: yes, setting prefetch_kv=false removes the issue. also toggling kv_shard_merge to single-shard removes repro (so it's a sharded-merge + async prefetch race).

ci-bot: build 2026.01.07-quantfuse-main completed (branch quant/async-prefetch) — tests: 218 passed, 7 flaky (longctx).

phil: likely root cause: we allocate tile slots and publish `seq` before the background prefetch finishes copying or before we increment the per-shard ptr atomically. fix options: (A) publish only after copy completes (hand-over token), (B) add atomic fetch_add for ptr, or (C) add a cheap seq slot check during merge to detect duplicates and discard out-of-order writes.
rana: prefer (A) + (C): only publish pointer after memcpy done to avoid stale reads, and defensive seq-check on merge. avoids a heavy global lock. add unit test that runs 100 concurrent prefetchers and asserts kv_ptr monotonicity.

elliot: I prototyped (A): gated publish after memcpy finishes. repro disappears locally. microbench: negligible perf hit on short runs, <1% on long streaming runs. will open PR.

phil: also add telemetry: kv_ptr_dup_total and kv_merge_seq_gap_total and an alert if either > 0.5/hour/node. capture a sampled trace with kv_ptr timeline if fired.

elliot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt-runtime/pull/4307 — includes guarded publish, seq-check in merge, repro script, unit test, and a longctx-quant CI job (runs to 40k tokens). tagging @oncall-ml for review.

ci-bot: PR 4307 opened by elliot. CI: quant-longctx queued.

sre-bot: found one customer incident (RD-3009) with duplicated tokens in a 38k generation trace; recommending expedited review and backport candidate if PR green.

rana: +1 for backport to 2025.12-stable with a rollout gate (enable prefetch_kv only when kv_ptr_dup_total == 0 sustained).

phil: can you include a micro-benchmark in the PR comparing publish-after-copy vs current and a short explanation of why it was safe w.r.t throughput? SRE wants numbers.

elliot: will add perf numbers and a short note. scheduling a 48h staging longctx run once CI passes. thanks all :thumbsup:
